summary: Democratic representative from Maryland since 2017 and a former American University constitutional-law professor and Maryland state senator. Days after burying his son, he was lead manager in Donald Trump's second impeachment trial in February 2021, which ended 57–43 for conviction, short of two-thirds; he then served on the January 6 committee. Since 2025 he has led House Judiciary Democrats against the Trump Justice Department, including a November 2025 report putting the Trump family's crypto holdings at up to $11.6 billion.

chapters.title: A constitutional-law professor from a political family
chapters.dek: Harvard, a Washington think-tank upbringing and 25 years teaching law.
chapters.body:
Raskin was born in Washington, D.C., on December 13, 1962. His father, Marcus Raskin, co-founded the Institute for Policy Studies [[wikipedia]]. His grandfather was the first Jewish member of the Minnesota legislature and "a very strong Zionist" who sent the grandchildren Israel bonds every birthday [[ji-2017]].

He graduated from Harvard College in 1983 and Harvard Law School in 1987, where he was an editor of the Harvard Law Review [[wikipedia, raskin-house-bio]]. From 1990 he taught constitutional law at American University's Washington College of Law for more than 25 years, wrote the student casebook We the Students and Overruling Democracy, a critique of the Supreme Court [[wikipedia, raskin-house-bio]].

chapters.title: Annapolis and the House
chapters.dek: Marriage equality, death-penalty repeal and a seat in Congress.
chapters.body:
Raskin served in the Maryland State Senate from 2007 to 2016, where colleagues elected him majority whip. He was a coalition-builder on marriage equality, abolition of the death penalty, the first benefit-corporation law in the country and Maryland's adoption of the National Popular Vote compact [[raskin-house-bio, wikipedia]].

He won Maryland's 8th congressional district in 2016 [[raskin-house-bio]]. That spring a humanist PAC had billed him as an open nontheist; he said, "I've never called myself an atheist" and described himself as "a humanist with a small 'h'" while remaining a member of Temple Sinai [[ap-humanist-2016]]. In 2018 he co-founded the Congressional Freethought Caucus [[wikipedia]].

chapters.title: Tommy, January 6 and the second impeachment
chapters.dek: A personal loss and a national crisis in the same week.
chapters.body:
Raskin's son Tommy died at the end of December 2020. The family buried him on January 5, and the next day Raskin's daughter and son-in-law were with him at the Capitol when rioters broke in [[amnews-2021, wikipedia]]. "I'm not going to lose my son at the end of 2020 and my country and my republic in 2021," he told CNN [[amnews-2021]].

As lead manager for Trump's second impeachment, opening the trial on February 9, 2021, he rejected the claim that a former president could not be tried, calling it "a brand new January exception to the Constitution," and told the Senate, "Senators, this cannot be our future" [[rev-opening-2021, amnews-2021]]. The Senate voted 57–43 to convict, short of the required two-thirds [[raskin-house-bio]]. He then sat on the January 6 select committee and delivered its criminal referral of Trump to the Justice Department, and in 2022 published Unthinkable, a memoir of those months that reached No. 1 on the New York Times list [[raskin-house-bio]].

chapters.title: Leading Judiciary Democrats against the Trump Justice Department
chapters.dek: Oversight, the Epstein files, crypto and the 25th Amendment.
chapters.body:
Raskin was diagnosed with lymphoma in December 2022, his second cancer after colon cancer in 2010, and said in April 2023 that it was in remission [[wikipedia]]. He served as the top Democrat on the Oversight Committee from 2023, and on December 18, 2024, the Democratic caucus unanimously chose him to lead its members on the Judiciary Committee after Jerry Nadler withdrew and endorsed him [[wikipedia, raskin-judiciary-2024]]. In January 2025 President Biden issued a preemptive pardon covering the January 6 committee's members, Raskin among them [[wikipedia]].

From the minority he has pursued the second Trump administration on several fronts. In November 2025 Judiciary Democrats estimated the Trump family's crypto holdings at up to $11.6 billion, with more than $800 million in sales in the first half of 2025; Raskin said Trump had "turned the Oval Office into the world's most corrupt crypto startup operation" [[judiciary-crypto-2025]]. In April 2026 he introduced a bill to create the presidential-capacity commission envisioned by the 25th Amendment, with 50 Democratic cosponsors [[raskin-25th-2026]]. That fall he pressed the Justice Department over its handling of investigations into Jeffrey Epstein's associates and asked the major platforms to enforce their rules against false claims about mail voting before the midterms [[judiciary-epstein-2026, judiciary-tech-2026]].
